title: Performance of the subcarrier-wave quantum key distribution in the presence of spontaneous Raman scattering noise generated by classical DWDM channels
authors: Fedor Kiselev, Roman Goncharov, Natalia Veselkova, Eduard Samsonov, Alexei D. Kiselev, Vladimir Egorov
abstract: In this paper we study performance of the subcarrier-wave quantum key distribution system (SCW QKD) in the presence of spontaneous Raman scattering (SpRS) noise generated by classical channels of dense wavelength division multiplexing (DWDM) network within a single-mode optical fiber. We present the mathematical model for evaluation of the quantum bit error rate (QBER) and the secure key generation rate with the SpRS noise taken into account. We consider two regimes of the SCW QKD system: the continuous wave regime that uses continuous wave laser and the pulsed regime. For these regimes, performance of the system is analyzed depending on receiver sensitivity of classical DWDM. It is found that the pulsed regime outperforms the continuous wave regime in both the secure key generation rate and the maximum achievable distance.
summary: This paper analyzes the performance limitations of Subcarrier-Wave Quantum Key Distribution (SCW QKD) when subjected to noise from classical DWDM traffic via spontaneous Raman scattering. By developing a detailed mathematical model, the authors compare continuous wave and pulsed operation modes. They conclusively show that operating in a pulsed regime significantly enhances both the secure key rate and the maximum transmission distance compared to the CW regime.
main_problem: The paper investigates how spontaneous Raman scattering (SpRS) noise, generated by classical Dense Wavelength Division Multiplexing (DWDM) channels, degrades the performance of Subcarrier-Wave Quantum Key Distribution (SCW QKD) systems.
main_result: The pulsed operational regime significantly outperforms the continuous wave (CW) regime, achieving both a higher secure key generation rate and a greater maximum achievable distance in the presence of this noise.
method: A mathematical model is developed to calculate the Quantum Bit Error Rate (QBER) and the secure key generation rate by incorporating the noise power from SpRS into the standard QKD analysis framework.
model_or_system: The system is an SCW QKD protocol operating over a single-mode optical fiber co-propagating with classical DWDM channels. The analysis compares performance in both continuous wave and pulsed laser regimes.
key_observables: Quantum Bit Error Rate (QBER), secure key generation rate, and maximum achievable distance.
important_parameters: Classical receiver sensitivity (ranging from -23 dBm to -48 dBm), DWDM parameters ($\xi = 0.18 	ext{ dB/km}$, $\Delta\lambda = 15 	ext{ GHz}$, $N_{ch} = 40$).
main_assumptions: The analysis assumes SpRS noise is evenly distributed in time for calculating the mean photon number, and it focuses on channels within the narrow spectral C-band.
figures_summary: Figure 5 compares the maximum possible operating distance versus classical channel receiver sensitivity for both CW and Pulsed modes, demonstrating the superior performance of the pulsed regime.
paper_structure: The paper first develops the mathematical framework to model SpRS noise impact, then analyzes the QBER and key rate for both CW and pulsed regimes, culminating in a comparison showing the pulsed regime's advantage across varying receiver sensitivities.
why_interesting: This work is highly relevant to quantum optics and open quantum systems as it models decoherence and noise (SpRS) from a realistic, high-power classical environment (DWDM) and proposes an operational regime (pulsed) to mitigate its detrimental effects on quantum communication.
